rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers should not be dazzled by disbelievers’ prosperity, worldly movement, or apparent success in different lands.
rows.anchor: لا تنظر إلى ما هم عليه من سعة الرزق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address may target the community through its leader, so the Prophet’s address functions as an address to all believers.
rows.anchor: مدرة القوم ومقدمهم يخاطب بشيء فيقوم خطابه مقام خطابهم جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the Prophet was never deceived; the warning reinforces his steadfastness and serves as admonition despite his protection from error.
rows.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان غير مغرور بحالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition against their worldly movement treats the cause as the means to prevent its result: if it deceived him, he would be deceived.
rows.anchor: وهذا من تنزيل السبب منزلة المسبب، لأن التقلب لو غره لاغتر به

rows.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق ويعقوب
rows.claim: They read the prohibitions with light nūn, as in la yagurrannaka and related forms.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي إسحاق ويعقوب: لا يغرنك ولا يصدنك ولا يصدنكم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والفراء وابن قتيبة والزجاج
rows.claim: They explain the disbelievers’ taqallub as their commercial travel and activity.
rows.anchor: تقلبهم: هو تصرفهم في التجارات قاله: ابن عباس، والفراء،

rows.speaker: عكرمة ومقاتل
rows.claim: They explain taqallub as the blessings that come to the disbelievers.
rows.anchor: أو ما يجري عليهم من النعم قاله: عكرمة، ومقاتل

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some exegetes explain it as their moving about without being seized for their sins.
rows.anchor: أو تصرفهم غير مأخوذين بذنوبهم قاله: بعض المفسرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their worldly enjoyment is little because it ends and disappears; their final abode is Hell.
rows.anchor: متاع قليل أي ذلك التقلب والتبسط شيء قليل متعوا به،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report cited from al-Tirmidhi compares worldly life within the Hereafter to what a person retrieves after dipping a finger into the sea.
rows.anchor: ما الدنيا في الآخرة إلا مثل ما يجعل أحدكم إصبعه في اليم فلينظر بم يرجع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report compares the Prophet and the world to a rider resting briefly under a tree before leaving it.
rows.anchor: ما مثلي ومثل الدنيا إلا كراكب قال في ظل شجرة في يوم حار

rows.speaker: أبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن
rows.claim: He explains ribāṭ as waiting for one prayer after another and says there was no military frontier post in the Prophet’s time.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن: الرباط انتظارا الصلاة بعد الصلاة

rows.speaker: أبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن
rows.claim: He adduces the Prophet’s report that ablution despite hardship, walking to mosques, and awaiting the next prayer erase sins and raise ranks; it calls this ribāṭ three times.
rows.anchor: إسباغ الوضوء على المكاره وكثرة الخطا إلى المساجد وانتظار الصلاة بعد الصلاة فذلكم الرباط ثلاثا

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: He says the correct lexical and legal meaning is remaining on the frontier for God, originally tied to horses; a frontier guard may be mounted or on foot.
rows.anchor: والقول الصحيح هو أن الرباط هو الملازمة في سبيل الله، أصلها من ربط الخيل

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: The prayer-waiting report only compares prayer-waiting with frontier service, since it too is a saving path; the literal meaning of ribāṭ is the frontier post.
rows.anchor: إنما هو تشبيه بالرباط في سبيل الله، إذ انتظار الصلاة إنما هو سبيل من السبل المنجية

rows.speaker: ابن المواز
rows.claim: Jurists define a murābiṭ as someone who travels to a frontier post and remains there for a period; permanent local residents who work there are not technically murābiṭūn.
rows.anchor: المرابط في سبيل الله عند الفقهاء هو الذي يشخص إلى ثغر من الثغور ليرابط فيه مدة ما

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He explains ṣābirū as matching or surpassing the enemy in patience and endurance under the hardships of battle.
rows.anchor: غالبوهم في الصبر على شدائد الحرب، لا تكونوا أقل صبرا منهم وثباتا

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He says the command to persist at the frontier follows the general command to be patient to stress the greater difficulty of this particular endurance.
rows.anchor: والمصابرة باب من الصبر، ذكر بعد الصبر على ما يجب الصبر عليه تحقيقا لشدته وصعوبته

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He reads rābiṭū as stationing horses at frontier posts, watchful and prepared to fight.
rows.anchor: وأقيموا في الثغور رباطين خيلكم فيها مترصدين مستعدين للغزو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Prophetic report promises that a day and night of frontier service equals a month of fasting and prayer, without breaking the fast or leaving prayer except for need.
rows.anchor: من رابط يوما وليلة في سبيل الله كان كعدل صيام شهر وقيامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muslim’s report says a day and night of frontier service is better than the world and its contents, and the guard’s provision and safety from the grave’s testers continue after death.
rows.anchor: رباط يوم وليلة خير من صيام شهر وقيامه وإن مات جرى عليه رزقه وأمن الفتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Dāwūd’s report says other people’s deeds end at death, while a frontier guard’s deeds keep growing until the Resurrection and he is protected from the grave’s testers.
rows.anchor: كل الميت يختم على عمله إلا المرابط فإنه ينمو له عمله إلى يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage uses taking the covenant metaphorically for accepting the obligations of the Torah and Gospel.
rows.anchor: عبر بأخذ الميثاق عن التزامهم أحكام ما أنزل عليهم من التوراة والإنجيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Throwing the scriptures behind their backs metaphorically means failing to act according to their rules; selling them cheaply means exchanging God’s signs for worldly goods by concealing them.
rows.anchor: وبالنبذ وراء ظهورهم عن ترك عملهم بمقتضى تلك الأحكام، وباشتراء ثمن قليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hearing the caller means receiving the commands, prohibitions, promise, and warning by responding; saying God does not waste deeds means that He rewards even small acts.
rows.anchor: وبسماع المنادي إن كان القرآن عن ما تلقوه من الأمر والنهي والوعد والوعيد بالاستجابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taqallub stands for people’s travel through the land in pursuit of livelihood, while bedding stands for the place where one settles.
rows.anchor: وبالتقلب عن ضربهم في الأرض لطلب المكاسب، وبالمهاد عن المكان المستقر فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nuzul metaphorically denotes the honors God hastens for the believers in Paradise, and speed metaphorically denotes hastening that honor.
rows.anchor: وبالسرعة التي هي حقيقة في المشي عن تعجيل كرامته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One proposed rhetorical reading takes ḥisāb as a metaphor for recompense, as in the expression ‘I did not know my account.’
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون الحساب استعير للجزاء، كما استعير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage identifies antithesis in explaining, people and concealing, heaven and earth, night and day, standing and sitting, and male and female.
rows.anchor: والطباق في: لتبيينه للناس ولا تكتمونه، وفي السموات والأرض، واختلاف الليل والنهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It identifies repetition in the repeated warnings and in five occurrences of ‘Our Lord,’ among other paired expressions.
rows.anchor: والتكرار: في لا تحسبن فلا تحسبنهم، وفي: ربنا في خمسة مواضع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It identifies restriction in ‘for people of understanding’ and several other phrases, and matching wordplay in ‘believed, so we believed.’
rows.anchor: والاختصاص في: لأولي الألباب، وفي: وما للظالمين من أنصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It begins a matching-wordplay example with ‘believed, so we believed.’
rows.anchor: والتجنيس المماثل في: أن آمنوا فآمنا، وفي:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rhetorical inventory continues with matching wordplay in ‘believe, so we believed’ and in ‘any worker among you.’
rows.anchor: عمل عامل منكم. والمغاير في: مناديا ينادي.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It identifies nonmatching wordplay between a caller and calling, an allusion in ‘You did not create this in vain,’ and ellipsis in several places.
rows.anchor: والمغاير في: مناديا ينادي. والإشارة في: ما خلقت هذا باطلا، والحذف في مواضع

none: This segment contains only the quoted verses, without commentary.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿIshra means companionship and mixing; the related verbs describe mutual social contact.
rows.anchor: العشرة: الصحبة والمخالطة. يقال: عاشروا، وتعاشروا، واعتشروا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ifḍāʾ means reaching an open, spacious place; the word is also used for people mixing and directly contacting each other.
rows.anchor: الإفضاء إلى الشيء: الوصول إلى فضاء منه، أي سعة غير محصورة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maqt is hatred joined with contempt, arising from a reprehensible act.
rows.anchor: المقت: البغض المقرون باستحقار حصل بسبب أمر قبيح ارتكبه صاحبه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An ʿamma is a father’s sister and a khāla is a mother’s sister; the alif in khāla derives from wāw, as related forms show.
rows.anchor: العمة: أخت الأب. الخالة: أخت الأم، وألفها منقلبة عن واو، دليل ذلك قولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A rabība is a man’s stepdaughter; ḥijr refers to the front of a garment and came to mean a child’s care and protection there.
rows.anchor: الربيبة: بنت زوج الرجل من غيره. الحجر بفتح الحاء وكسرها: مقدم ثوب الإنسان وما بين يديه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥalīla means wife and ḥalīl means husband; the author derives the wife’s name from dwelling wherever her husband settles.
rows.anchor: الحليلة: الزوجة، والحليل الزوج قال: أغشى فتاة الحي عند حليلها

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: He derives ḥalīla from ḥalāl, meaning that she is made lawful; another explanation says each spouse makes the other’s waistcloth lawful.
rows.anchor: وذهب الزجاج وغيره إلى أنها من لفظ الحلال، فهي حليلة بمعنى محللة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣulb means the back, with ṣalība denoting strength and firmness.
rows.anchor: الصلب: الظهر، وصلب صلابة قوي واشتد.

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: He reports regional pronunciation: Hijaz speakers say ṣulb with a rounded vowel, while Tamim and Asad say ṣalb with open vowels, citing verse evidence.
rows.anchor: أن الصلب وهو الظهر، على وزن قفل هو لغة أهل الحجاز ويقول فيه تميم وأسد:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poet’s line using ṣulb is cited as evidence for the regional pronunciation.
rows.anchor: وصلب مثل العنان المؤدم ... قال وأنشدني بعض بني أسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muḥṣan describes a chaste woman who protects herself from suspicion; iḥṣān fundamentally means protection or restraint.
rows.anchor: المحصنة: المرأة العفيفة. يقال: أحصنت فهي محصن، وحصنت فهي حصان عفت عن الريبة

rows.speaker: شمر
rows.claim: He gives ḥaṣān and ḥāṣin as forms for a chaste woman and cites poetry about women protected from harm and sexual misconduct.
rows.anchor: وقال شمر: يقال امرأة حصان، وحاصن.

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: He records ḥaṣāna as the verbal noun, while Abū ʿUbayda and al-Kisāʾī use another form.
rows.anchor: ومصدر حصنت حصن. قال سيبويه: وقال أبو عبيدة والكسائي: حصانة.

rows.speaker: ثعلب عن ابن الأعرابي
rows.claim: He reports the unusual active participle pattern mufʿil for verbs such as aḥṣana, ashhaba, and abʿaja.
rows.anchor: ويقال في اسم الفاعل من أحصن وأسهب وأبعج، مفعل بفتح عين الكلمة، وهو شذوذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sifāḥ means illicit sex, named from spilling because each partner spills semen.
rows.anchor: المسافحة والسفاح: الزنا، وأصله من السفح وهو الصب، يسفح كل من الزانيين نطفته.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A khidn or khadīn is a companion or lover.
rows.anchor: الخدن والخدين: الصاحب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭawl means surplus or advantage; the expression ṭāla ʿalayhi means that one had an advantage over him.
rows.anchor: الطول: الفضل، يقال منه: طال عليه يطول طولا فضل عليه.

rows.speaker: الليث والزجاج
rows.claim: They explain ṭawl as capacity or ability, alongside the author’s gloss of surplus and advantage.
rows.anchor: وقال الليث والزجاج: الطول القدرة. انتهى. ويقال له: عليه طول أي زيادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cited line uses ṭāʾil for one lacking increase or merit, illustrating the lexical gloss of ṭawl as surplus.
rows.anchor: لقد زادني حبا لنفسي أنني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The related word for a young woman derives from youth; al-Jawālīqī calls a pubescent girl a young woman and a servant a young man.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن منصور الجواليقي: المتفتية والفتاة المراهقة، والفتى الرفيق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Prophetic report recommends saying ‘my young man’ or ‘my young woman’ rather than ‘my slave’ or ‘my female slave.’
rows.anchor: لا يقل أحدكم عبدي ولا أمتي ولكن ليقل فتاي وفتاتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-mayl means deviation from a straight path, introducing the discussion of women who commit indecency.
rows.anchor: الميل: العدول عن طريق الاستواء.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: He interprets the indecency committed by women as lesbianism and assigns them confinement until death or marriage.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد واختاره أبو مسلم بن بحر الأصبهاني: هذه الآية نزلت في النساء.

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم بن بحر الأصبهاني
rows.claim: He reads 4:15 as female same-sex conduct and 4:16 as male same-sex conduct, unlike the majority’s reading of both as adultery; he denies abrogation in the Quran.
rows.anchor: قال: ونزلت والذان يأتيانها منكم في أهل اللواط. والتي في النور: في الزانية والزاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verses fit the prior commands about women by prescribing a severe, ultimately benevolent safeguard for their afterlife and preventing the idea that kindness means omitting penalties.
rows.anchor: وفي الحقيقة هو إحسان إليهن، إذ هو نظر في أمر آخرتهن، ولئلا يتوهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening marriage rules lead into penalties for those who violate them through illicit sex; women are first singled out, then included with male adulterers.
rows.anchor: فكان في مبدأ السورة التحصن بالتزويج، وإباحة ما أباح من نكاح أربع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation for mentioning women first is that they are more driven by sexual desire than men.
rows.anchor: لأنهن على ما قيل أدخل في باب الشهوة من الرجال، ثم ذكرهن ثانيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Allatī is a plural by meaning of allatī and has several plurals, with al-lāʾāt the strangest; its declension resembles Hindāt.
rows.anchor: واللاتي جمع من حيث المعنى للتي، ولها جموع كثيرة أغربها: اللاآت،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaʾtīna al-fāḥisha means they commit or engage in the deed; most exegetes identify the fāḥisha here as adultery, with Mujahid’s dissent noted.
rows.anchor: ومعنى يأتين الفاحشة: يجئن ويغشين. والفاحشة هنا الزنا بإجماع من المفسرين،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name fāḥisha is applied to adultery because it exceeds many other acts in repulsiveness; a proposed account ranks sexual corruption as the lowest faculty’s corruption.
rows.anchor: وأطلق على الزنا اسم الفاحشة لزيادتها في القبح على كثير من القبائح.

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: He argues that the women-versus-men wording is restrictive, avoids abrogation and repetition, and permits interpreting the later path as marriage for women who commit lesbianism.
rows.anchor: وحجة أبي مسلم في أن الفاحشة هي السحاق قوله: واللاتي يأتين الفاحشة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent wording supports Mujahid and others: the first verse covers all women, married or unmarried, and the second all males, married or unmarried, while the light and heavy penalties divide the sexes.
rows.anchor: والذي يقتضيه ظاهر اللفظ هو قول مجاهد وغيره: أن اللاتي مختص بالنساء، وهو عام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says same-sex conduct existed among Arabs, though rarely, and cites lines by Ṭarafa and a rajaz poet as evidence.
rows.anchor: لا يقال: إن السحاق واللواط لم يكونا معروفين في العرب ولا في الجاهلية،

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: He reads the phrase with an added bi, ‘who commit the indecency,’ rather than the standard wording.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله: واللاتي يأتين بالفاحشة، وقوله: من نسائكم اختلف،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegetes differ whether ‘your women’ means wives, free women, Muslim women, or previously married women; Qatada and al-Suddi are named for the first view.
rows.anchor: اختلف، هل المراد الزوجات أو الحرائر أو المؤمنات أو الثيبات دون الأبكار؟

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: He says the possessive ‘your’ marks affiliation with Islam, since a non-Muslim wife may be attributed to Muslims without falling under this rule.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: قوله من نسائكم إضافة في معنى الإسلام، لأن الكافرة قد تكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent and predominant usage of ‘your women’ means wives, and most exegetes hold that the verse concerns wives.
rows.anchor: وكون المراد الزوجات وأن الآية فيهم، هو قول أكثر المفسرين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Requiring four witnesses makes the accusation difficult to prove and helps conceal the sin; another view assigns two witnesses to each act.
rows.anchor: وأمر تعالى باستشهاد أربعة تغليظا على المدعي، وسترا لهذه المعصية. وقيل:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The witness requirement appears limited to Muslim men; testimony may be given after directly seeing adultery, without loss of probity when looking was for that purpose.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أنه يختص بالذكور المؤمنين لقوله: أربعة منكم، وأنه يجوز الاستشهاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Allatī is the subject and the command is its predicate; the relative clause meets the conditions that allow a predicate introduced by fa like a conditional clause.
rows.anchor: وإعراب اللاتي مبتدأ، وخبره فاستشهدوا. وجاز دخول الفاء في الخبر،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the relative clause behaves like a conditional, the verb cannot be parsed as a governing verb for an omitted-fronted object in an object-preposing construction.
rows.anchor: فلا يجوز أن ينتصب بإضمار فعل يفسره فاستشهدوا، فيكون من باب الاشتغال،

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: He allows an omitted predicate such as ‘the ruling of those women is recited to you,’ paralleling his treatment of the thief and female thief clauses.
rows.anchor: كقول سيبويه في قوله: والسارق والسارقة وفي قوله: الزانية والزاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min nisaʾikum may depend on an omitted phrase describing the women as belonging to the addressees; minkum may modify the witness command or describe the four witnesses.
rows.anchor: ويتعلق من نسائكم بمحذوف، لأنه في موضع حال من الفاعل في: يأتين، تقديره:

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The report from ʿUbāda in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim explains the path as stoning for a previously married offender and one hundred lashes plus exile for a virgin.
rows.anchor: «البكر بالبكر جلد مائة وتغريب عام، والثيب بالثيب» رمي بالحجارة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report clarifies the confinement verse’s unspecified future path; it does not abrogate it, but specifies the general flogging rule.
rows.anchor: حديث عبادة ليس بناسخ لهذه الآية، ولا لأنه الجلد، بل هو مبين لمجمل في هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects al-Rāzī’s charge that al-Shāfiʿī’s view requires Quran–Sunna and Sunna–Quran abrogation; explanation and specification avoid that claim.
rows.anchor: بل البيان والتخصيص أولى من ادعاء نسخ ثلاث مرات على ما ذهب إليه أصحاب أبي حنيفة،

rows.speaker: مجاهد وأبو مسلم
rows.claim: They interpret the paired masculine form and ‘from you’ as referring to male homosexual conduct.
rows.anchor: تقدم قول مجاهد واختيار أبي مسلم أنها في اللواطة، ويؤيده ظاهر التثنية.

rows.speaker: جمهور المفسرين
rows.claim: The majority read the pair as male and female adulterers, using a masculine dual to include a woman with a man.
rows.anchor: والجمهور على أنها في الزناة الذكور والإناث. واللذان أريد به الزاني والزانية،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The harm command follows proof of the act, whose evidence is specified in the previous verse; harm can be verbal, physical, or both.
rows.anchor: وترتب الأذى على إتيان الفاحشة وهو مقيد بالشهادة على إتيانها. وبين ذلك في الآية السابقة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He defines the harm as verbal and manual abuse, striking with sandals, and similar treatment.
rows.anchor: هو النيل باللسان واليد، وضرب النعال وما أشبهه.

rows.speaker: قتادة والسدي
rows.claim: They interpret the harm as reproach and rebuke.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة والسدي: هو التعبير والتوبيخ.

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some say the commanded harm is physical action without speech; another group says it is insult and estrangement without reproach.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: بالفعل دون القول. وقالت فرقة: هو السب والجفا دون تعيير.

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: He reads harm as combining the two legal penalties, lashes and stoning, and applied both to the Hamdani woman.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الأذى المأمور به هو الجمع بين الحدين: الجلد والرجم، وهو قول علي،

rows.speaker: قتادة والسدي وابن زيد
rows.claim: They distinguish married women in the first verse from unmarried men and women in the second; al-Ṭabarī preferred this reading.
rows.anchor: هي في الرجل والمرأة البكرين، وأما الأولى ففي النساء المزوجات، ويدخل معهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority say both earlier penalties were superseded by the flogging verse, except on readings that retain Ali’s combined penalty or reproach together with flogging.
rows.anchor: وأجمعوا على أن هاتين الآيتين منسوختان بآية الجلد، إلا في تفسير علي الأذى فلا نسخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the adultery reading, the woman receives both confinement and shared harm; confinement is explained as containing her misconduct, while men need to work outside.
rows.anchor: فيكون الإيذاء مشتركا بينهما، والحبس مختص بالمرأة فيجمع عليها الحبس والإيذاء،

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: He places the confinement verse after the harm verse, applying it to unrepentant offenders, but the author rejects this as disrupting the order.
rows.anchor: وذهب الحسن إلى أن هذه الآية قبل الآية المتقدمة، ثم نزل فأمسكوهن في البيوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repentance is obligatory by the community’s consensus and remains valid even if the person later repeats that or another sin, contrary to Muʿtazilites and similar dissenters.
rows.anchor: والتوبة فرض بإجماع الأمة، وتصح وإن نقضها في ثاني حال بمعاودة الذنب

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: He says ʿalā can mean ʿinda, ‘at’ or ‘with.’
rows.anchor: وقيل: على بمعنى عند. وقال الحسن: بمعنى من، والسوء يعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-sūʾ includes disbelief and other sins and is named for the bad outcome it brings.
rows.anchor: والسوء يعم الكفر والمعاصي غيره سمي بذلك لأنه تسوء عاقبته.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He takes ‘in ignorance’ as a state of folly in which desire overcomes reason, since reason calls to obedience and appetite to disobedience; every sinner is ignorant in this sense.
rows.anchor: إذ ارتكاب السوء، لا يكون إلا عن غلبة الهوى للعقل، والعقل يدعو إلى الطاعة،

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: He takes ignorance here to mean deliberate action, but the author rejects that reading because Muslims agree that deliberate sinners who repent are forgiven.
rows.anchor: كما ذهب إليه الضحاك. وروي عن مجاهد لإجماع المسلمين: على أن من تعمد الذنب وتاب،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Companions agreed that every sin is committed in ignorance, whether intentionally or unknowingly.
rows.anchor: وأجمع أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على أن كل معصية هي بجهالة عمدا كانت أو جهلا.

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: He says sinners know the act is sinful but do not know the full nature of its punishment.
rows.anchor: لا يجهل كونها معصية، ولكن لا يعلم كنه العقوبة.

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: He calls worldly preoccupation ignorance because it pulls a person away from obedience to God.
rows.anchor: أمور الدنيا كلها جهالة، يعني ما اختص بها وخرج عن طاعة الله.

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: He explains ignorance as preferring fleeting pleasure and immediate advantage to lasting pleasure and future reward.
rows.anchor: جهالته من حيث آثر اللذة الفانية على اللذة الباقية، والحظ العاجل على الآجل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations take ignorance as persistence, or as acting without persistence so that the act resembles an unintentional mistake.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الجهالة الإصرار على المعصية، ولذلك عقبه بقوله: ثم يتوبون من قريب.

rows.speaker: الماتريدي
rows.claim: He allows accidental wrongdoing or intentional wrongdoing through ignorance of its prohibition or degree, but excludes deliberate contempt or trivialization.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل قصد الفعل والجهل بموقعه أي: أنه حرام، أو في الحرمة: أي: قدر هي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ignorance may also involve acting under desire while expecting future repentance, presuming forgiveness, or not knowing the punishment.
rows.anchor: وقد تكون الجهالة جهالة عقوبة عليه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Soon’ may mean before death’s rattle, before sins outweigh good deeds, or before accumulated sins darken the heart and lead to comprehensive disbelief.
rows.anchor: أي من زمان قريب. والقرب هنا بالنسبة إلى زمان المعصية، وهي بقية مدة حياته إلى أن يغرغر،

rows.speaker: عكرمة والضحاك ومحمد بن قيس وأبو مجلز وابن زيد
rows.claim: They define ‘soon’ as before the angels appear and death’s agony begins; Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Suddī instead say before illness and death.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة والضحاك ومحمد بن قيس وأبو مجلز وابن زيد وغيرهم: قبل المعاينة للملائكة والسوق.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He says repentance should occur before the authority of death descends; the author calls Ibn ʿAbbās’s timing the best opportunity and the preceding views the last opportunity.
rows.anchor: فذكر ابن عباس أحسن أوقات التوبة، وذكر من قبله آخر وقتها.

rows.speaker: أبو أيوب
rows.claim: He transmits from the Prophet that God accepts a servant’s repentance until the soul rattles in the throat.
rows.anchor: وروى أبو أيوب عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إن الله يقبل توبة العبد ما لم يغرغر»

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: A report says Iblis vowed to persist in tempting Adam’s descendants while their souls remain in their bodies, and God swore He would keep repentance open until death rattles.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن أن إبليس قال حين أهبط إلى الأرض: وعزتك لا أفارق ابن آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The period is called near because the appointed term is coming, life is short, and people expect death at any moment.
rows.anchor: وسميت هذه المدة قريبة لأن الأجل آت، وكل ما هو آت قريب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preferred syntax makes repentance the subject, ‘upon God’ its predicate, and ‘for those who’ dependent on that predicate; he rejects Abu al-Baqāʾ’s elaborate alternatives.
rows.anchor: وارتفاع التوبة على الابتداء، والخبر هو على الله، وللذين متعلق بما يتعلق به على الله،

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: He offers alternative syntactic parses for the predicate and the attachment of ‘for those who,’ which the author says needlessly complicate the construction.
rows.anchor: وأجاز أبو البقاء أن يكون الخبر للذين، ويتعلق على الله بمحذوف،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bi-jahāla may be causal: ignorance drives the sinner, since someone fully aware of the consequence would not act; reason is then overcome or absent.
rows.anchor: ويجوز عندي أن تكون باء السبب أي الحامل لهم على عمل السوء هو الجهالة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min qarīb may be partitive, meaning repentance in any part of a nearby period, or mark the starting point of repentance soon after the sin to prevent persistence.
rows.anchor: وفيها وجهان: أحدهما: أنها للتبعيض، أي بعض زمان قريب،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second parse implies that a long-delayed repentant falls outside the group singled out for God’s special promise, though the verse does not say repentance is impossible.
rows.anchor: أنه لو تاب من زمان بعيد فإنه يخرج عن من خص بكرامة ختم قبول التوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Basran grammarians reject min marking the beginning of a time period; omitting the noun ‘time’ and retaining qarīb as its substitute is also not a regular construction.
rows.anchor: ودخول من الابتدائية على الزمان لا يجيزه البصريون، وحذف الموصوف هنا وهو زمان،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated promise that God turns to repentants uses different prepositions to suit different meanings: accepting repentance upon Himself and showing mercy to them.
rows.anchor: ولما ضمن يتوب معنى ما يعدى بعلى عداه بعلى، كأنه قال: يعطف عليهم.

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He says ‘repentance upon God’ declares that acceptance is incumbent, while ‘God turns to them’ promises certain fulfillment, reflecting Muʿtazilite doctrine.
rows.anchor: إعلام بوجوبها عليه، كما يجب على العبد بعض الطاعات.

rows.speaker: محمد بن عمر الرازي
rows.claim: He reads the first clause as a guaranteed act of beneficence rather than an entitlement, and the second as God’s promise to act; alternatively, the first is guidance and the second acceptance.
rows.anchor: إن قوله: إنما التوبة على الله إعلام بأنه يجب قبولها لزوم إحسان لا استحقاق،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is all-knowing of obedience and disobedience and wise in placing things properly, so He accepts the repentance of those who return.
rows.anchor: أي عليما بمن يطيع ويعصي، حكيما أي: يضع الأشياء مواضعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse denies acceptance to the sinner who delays repentance until despair at death, and to the person who dies in disbelief; Pharaoh is an example of the first.
rows.anchor: نفى تعالى أن يكون التوبة للعاصي الصائر في حيز اليأس من الحياة، ولا للذي وافى على الكفر.

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He equates the deathbed with the afterlife because both lie beyond the point of choice and religious responsibility.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: سوى بين الذين سوفوا توبتهم إلى حضرة الموت،

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: They say knowledge of God becomes necessary through witnessing afterlife terrors, removing the basis for religious obligation and choice.
rows.anchor: زعمت المعتزلة أن العلم بالله في دار التكليف يجوز أن يكون نظريا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says approaching death does not itself end responsibility: Israelites were resurrected and held accountable after death, and death’s pain is no greater than other severe pain.
rows.anchor: أن القرب من الموت لا يمنع من قبول التوبة، لأن جماعة من بني إسرائيل أماتهم الله، ثم أحياهم وكلفهم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Near-death distress could even help a person repent; God may accept at some times and withhold acceptance at others by sovereign choice.
rows.anchor: ولأنه عند القرب يصير مضطرا فيكون ذلك سببا للقبول، ولكنه تعالى يفعل ما يشاء.

rows.speaker: الربيع
rows.claim: He says the verse originally concerned Muslims and was superseded by the statement that God may forgive lesser sins, leaving believers’ fate to divine will.
rows.anchor: نزلت وليست التوبة في المسلمين، ثم نسخها: إن الله لا يغفر أن يشرك به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says no abrogation need be claimed: 4:18 does not say that no sinner without accepted repentance can be forgiven; he also notes that reports are not normally abrogated.
rows.anchor: وطعن على ابن زيد: بأن الآية خبر، والأخبار لا تنسخ.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two coordinated groups are distinct: ‘nor’ negates the rule separately for each group, and the phrase ‘while they are unbelievers’ belongs to those who die in that state.
rows.anchor: وظاهر قوله: ولا الذين يموتون وهم كفار أن هؤلاء مغايرون لقوله: للذين يعملون السيئات،

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī gives two readings of those doing sins: disbelievers, because the next clause says they die as unbelievers, or Muslim grave sinners, with unbelief used as severe threat language.
rows.anchor: فيه وجهان: أحدهما: أن يراد به الكفار لظاهر قوله: وهم كفار، وأن يراد الفساق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author calls al-Zamakhsharī’s options contradictory: his earlier explanation requires two groups, but this discussion collapses them into one or treats unbelief figuratively.
rows.anchor: وهو في غاية الاضطراب، لأنه قبل ذلك حمل الآية على أنها دالة على قسمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says the strained interpretation serves Muʿtazilite doctrine by guaranteeing punishment for grave sinners and violates syntax and the apparent sense.
rows.anchor: انتصار لمذهبه حتى يرتب العذاب: إما للكافر، وإما للفاسق، فخرج بذلك عن قوانين النحو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The present tense ‘they do’ signals persistence in sins until death; ‘I repent now’ is repentance only upon seeing death and is therefore defensive, not accepted.
rows.anchor: وجاء يعملون بصيغة المضارع لا بصيغة الماضي إشعارا بأنهم مصرون على عمل السيئات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading makes ‘I repent now’ conditional rather than decisive, which is why it is not accepted.
rows.anchor: وقيل: قوله تبت الآن توبة شريطية فلم تقبل، لأنه لم يقطع بها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Repentance is not for them’ means their repentance is not accepted, not that they cannot repent; the second group literally dies in disbelief and cannot repent afterward in this world.
rows.anchor: وقوله: وليست التوبة ظاهره النفي لوجودها، والمعنى على نفي القبول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘They die’ may mean they approach death, just as ‘death came’ can refer to its signs; then unbelief, like repentance, is not accepted at that point.
rows.anchor: بقوله: يموتون، يقربون من الموت كما في قوله: حضر أحدهم الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Those’ may refer to both groups, who share a prepared punishment though one punishment ends and the other lasts forever, or only to the nearest-mentioned unbelievers.
rows.anchor: يحتمل أن تكون الإشارة إلى الصنفين، ويكونان قد شركا في إعداد العذاب لهما،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first reading warns the sinner who delays repentance until death by pairing him with an unbeliever; the second ties the threat to dying in disbelief.
rows.anchor: ويكون ذلك وعيدا للعاصي الذي لم يتب إلا عند معاينة الموت حيث شرك بينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent mention of punishment already prepared indicates that Hell is created, a topic the author says he discussed earlier.
rows.anchor: وظاهر الإعداد أن النار مخلوقة وسبق الكلام على ذلك.

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He says the parallel wording of a prepared threat and God’s promise to accept repentance shows both outcomes will certainly occur.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: أولئك أعتدنا لهم في الوعيد، نظير قوله: فأولئك يتوب الله عليهم في الوعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says this subtly imports the Muʿtazilite claim that grave sinners without repentance must certainly be punished; the nearest antecedent may instead be unbelievers.
rows.anchor: وتلطف الزمخشري في دسه الاعتزال هنا، وذلك أنه كان قد قرر أول كلامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if the threat includes unrepentant Muslim sinners, it does not require punishment: God may punish or forgive them under the decisive verse about lesser sins.
rows.anchor: إذ يجوز العقاب ويجوز العفو. وفائدة وروده حصول التخويف للفاسق.

rows.speaker: أبو قلابة والحسن
rows.claim: They identify the fāḥisha in the exception as adultery; al-Ḥasan says an unmarried adulteress receives one hundred lashes and a year’s exile and returns what she took from her husband.
rows.anchor: والفاحشة هنا الزنا قاله: أبو قلابة والحسن. قال الحسن: إذا زنت البكر جلدت مائة

rows.speaker: أبو قلابة
rows.claim: He says a husband may pressure and mistreat a wife who commits adultery so she will ransom herself from him.
rows.anchor: إذا زنت امرأة الرجل فلا بأس أن يضارها ويشق عليها حتى تفتدي منه.

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: He says husbands may take their wives’ dowries if they commit that act.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: إذا فعلن ذلك فخذوا مهورهن.

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: He says this rule applied earlier and was superseded by the fixed legal penalties.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء: كان هذا الحكم ثم نسخ بالحدود.

rows.speaker: ابن سيرين وأبو قلابة
rows.claim: They say a husband may not use divorce compensation until another man is found on his wife.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن سيرين وأبو قلابة: لا يحل الخلع حتى يوجد رجل على بطنها.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: He says a husband may not harm his wife to force compensation from her, even if she commits adultery.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: لا يحل له أن يحبسها ضرارا حتى تفتدي منه، يعني: وإن زنت.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وعائشة والضحاك
rows.claim: They interpret the fāḥisha as a wife’s disobedience or marital rebellion, which permits taking her money; the author identifies this as Mālik’s position.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وعائشة والضحاك وغيرهم: الفاحشة هنا النشوز، فإذا نشزت حل له

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Others interpret the fāḥisha as foul speech or bad treatment, equivalent to disobedience, permitting compensation when the wife is at fault.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: الفاحشة البذاء باللسان وسوء العشرة قولا وفعلا وهذا في معنى النشوز.

rows.speaker: أبي وابن مسعود
rows.claim: Their variant readings add ‘against you’ or ‘and live with you,’ supporting the bad-conduct interpretation; the author treats these as explanatory readings, not Quranic text.
rows.anchor: قراءة أبي: إلا أن يفحشن عليكم، وقراءة ابن مسعود: إلا أن يفحشن وعاشروهن،

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: He allows a husband to take all the wealth of a disobedient wife, while another view limits him to some of what he gave her.
rows.anchor: وقال مالك: للزوج أن يأخذ من الناشز جميع ما تملكه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception’s apparent meaning permits coercion to obtain some of what was given, or even money not given, when a wife commits manifest immorality.
rows.anchor: وظاهر الاستثناء يقتضي إباحة العضل له ليذهب ببعض ما أعطاها

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو بكر
rows.claim: They read mubayyinah with an open yāʾ, meaning the claimant makes the alleged act clear; others read it with a kasra, meaning clear in itself.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو بكر: مبينة هنا، وفي الأحزاب، والطلاق بفتح الياء،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers parsing the prohibition of ʿaḍl as a jussive clause coordinated with the preceding command, and rejects Ibn ʿAṭiyya’s accusative analysis.
rows.anchor: وظاهر قوله: ولا تعضلوهن، أن لا نهي، فالفعل مجزوم بها،

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: His reading adds an and before ‘that you prevent them,’ strengthening the possibility of an accusative construction and showing that ʿaḍl is textually forbidden.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود: ولا أن تعضلوهن، فهذه القراءة تقوي احتمال النصب،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects Ibn ʿAṭiyya’s syntax: with a negated verb, an omitted subjunctive marker belongs after the coordinator, not after lā; the proposed parse confuses verb coordination with noun-source coordination.
rows.anchor: فالمعنى: أريد التوبة وانتفاء دخولي النار. فلو كان الفعل المتسلط على المتعاطفين منفيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to live with wives honorably is addressed to husbands and requires fairness in lodging and maintenance and gracious speech, correcting their customary mistreatment.
rows.anchor: وعاشروهن بالمعروف هذا أمر بحسن المعاشرة، والظاهر أنه أمر للأزواج، لأن التلبس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disliking a wife must not lead to mistreatment: what one dislikes may benefit religion and the final outcome, as 2:216 similarly teaches.
rows.anchor: فإن كرهتموهن فعسى أن تكرهوا شيئا ويجعل الله فيه خيرا كثيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in ‘He places good in it’ may refer to the disliked thing, dislike itself, or patience; Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Suddī give righteous offspring as an illustration, not an exclusive meaning.
rows.anchor: وفسر ابن عباس والسدي: الخير بالولد الصالح، وهو على سبيل التمثيل لا الحصر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording’s generic ‘something’ rather than ‘them’ urges keeping wives and companionship despite disliked traits, leading into the discussion of replacing a wife.
rows.anchor: وسياق الآية يدل على أن المعنى الحث على إمساكهن وعلى صحبتهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intimacy between spouses means the prohibition covers taking anything given to a wife, not merely her dowry, whether it was a dowry or something else.
rows.anchor: أفضى بعضكم إلى بعض لأن هذا لا يقتضي أن يكون الذي آتاها مهرا فقط،

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الرازي
rows.claim: He argues that a broad opening clause may be followed by a narrower rule without making the opening wording itself specific.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو بكر الرازي: لا يمتنع أن يكون أول الخطاب عموما في جميع ما تضمنه الاسم،

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الرازي
rows.claim: He applies the verse to advance maintenance when a wife dies before the paid period ends, saying her husband cannot reclaim it from her inheritance.
rows.anchor: قال أبو بكر الرازي: وفي الآية دليل على أن من أسلف امرأته نفقتها لمدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects that analogy because replacing a wife presupposes both the old wife and her substitute are present; death leaves no one to replace.
rows.anchor: وليس بظاهر لأن الاستبدال يقتضي وجود البدل والمبدل منه، أما إذا كان قد عدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The condition is not restrictive: it names the situation where a husband might think a replacement lets him reclaim the first wife’s gift; intimacy makes the ban even stronger when their marriage continues.
rows.anchor: ومفهوم الشرط غير مراد، وإنما خص بالذكر لأنها حالة قد يتوهم فيها

rows.speaker: أبو السمال وأبو جعفر
rows.claim: They read shayʾan with a fatḥa and tanwīn on the yāʾ, deleting the hamza and transferring its vowel to the yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو السمال وأبو جعفر: شيا بفتح الياء وتنوينها، حذف الهمزة وألقى حركتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Buhtān originally means a lie confronted to its target so that the person is bewildered; it then came to mean any glaring falsehood.
rows.anchor: أصل البهتان: الكذب الذي يواجه به الإنسان صاحبه على جهة المكابرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question is a rebuke; men commonly falsely accused wives of sexual misconduct to frighten them into surrendering their dowry.
rows.anchor: وهذا الاستفهام على سبيل الإنكار، أي: أتفعلون هذا مع ظهور قبحه؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation calls it buhtān because reclaiming the gift implies the husband falsely says he never gave it; grammatically the terms may be circumstantial or purposive accusatives.
rows.anchor: وقيل: سمي بهتانا لأنه كان فرض لها المهر، واسترداده يدل على أنه يقول: لم أفرضه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If mā can refer to individual rational beings, the phrase means women whom fathers married; the Companions used it to prohibit marrying a father’s wife.
rows.anchor: وقد زعم أنه مذهب سيبويه. وعلى هذا المفهوم من إطلاق ما على منكوحات الآباء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He says pre-Islamic Arabs forbade many relations except a father’s wife and combining two sisters; any woman the father married is forbidden, whether he consummated the marriage or not.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: كان أهل الجاهلية يحرمون ما يحرم إلا امرأة الأب، والجمع بين الأختين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another analysis takes mā as a verbal noun: the prohibition concerns imitating the corrupt or forbidden marriage customs practiced by the fathers.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: ما مصدرية. والتقدير: ولا تنكحوا نكاح آبائكم أي: مثل نكاح آبائكم الفاسد،

rows.speaker: محمد بن جرير
rows.claim: He prefers the verbal-noun analysis, arguing that if the verse meant the women fathers married it should have said man rather than mā.
rows.anchor: واختار هذا القول محمد بن جرير قال: ولو كان معناه ولا تنكحوا النساء اللاتي نكح آباؤكم،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وعكرمة وقتادة وعطاء
rows.claim: They understand nikāḥ here as intercourse, reflecting the custom of inheriting a father’s wives.
rows.anchor: وحمل ابن عباس وعكرمة وقتادة وعطاء النكاح هنا على الوطء، لأنهم كانوا يرثون نكاح نسائهم.

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: He and a group understand it as a valid marriage contract, not fornication.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد في جماعة: المراد به العقد الصحيح، لا ما كان منهم بالزنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the contract reading, ‘except what has passed’ is disconnected and removes liability for pre-prohibition conduct; Ibn Zayd instead treats prior adultery by fathers as the exception.
rows.anchor: والاستثناء في قوله: إلا ما قد سلف منقطع، إذ لا يجامع الاستقبال الماضي، والمعنى:

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: On his alternative intercourse reading, the exception is connected: a son may marry a woman his father had only fornicated with before Islam.
rows.anchor: فعلى هذا يكون إلا ما قد سلف استثناء متصلا، إذ ما قد سلف مندرج تحت قوله: ما نكح

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: He explains the exception as God’s remission of what occurred before the prohibition.
rows.anchor: وقال الأخفش المعنى: فإنكم تعذبون به إلا ما قد سلف، فقد وضعه الله عنكم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects the proposed fronting and postponement of the exception as grammatically and semantically incoherent: it would make past conduct an exception to past repulsiveness.
rows.anchor: والذي يظهر من الآية أن كل امرأة نكحها أبو الرجل بعقد أو ملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception cannot precede its governing clause, and the construction would imply that the past incestuous act was not repulsive, an impossible meaning.
rows.anchor: أما من حيث المعنى فإنه أخبر أنه فاحشة ومقت في الزمان الماضي، فلا يصح أن يستثنى منه الماضي،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent rule forbids a man from marrying, by contract or ownership, any woman his father married; here nikāḥ means lawful intercourse, not fornication.
rows.anchor: كل امرأة نكحها أبو الرجل بعقد أو ملك فإنه يحرم عليه أن ينكحها بعقد أو ملك

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He interprets the impossible exception as rhetorical intensification: marry the past cases if possible, which cannot be done, to close any route to permission.
rows.anchor: والغرض المبالغة في تحريمه وسد الطريق إلى إباحته، كما يعلق بالمحال في التأبيد

rows.speaker: محمد بن عمر الرازي
rows.claim: He raises six objections to deriving the full prohibition from the verse alone: its passive form, possible temporary scope, addressed audience, past tense, apparent all-to-all reading, and suggestion of prior permissibility.
rows.anchor: وقال محمد بن عمر الرازي: فيها عندي بحث من وجوه: أحدها: أن بناء الفعل للمفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says these objections are unhelpful: the omitted agent is known to be God, and surrounding clauses confirm the divine source of prohibition and permission.
rows.anchor: ومعلوم أن المحرم هو الله تعالى. ألا ترى إلى آخر الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine prohibition implies permanence unless the text specifies a temporary exception, as it does for necessity.
rows.anchor: ومتى جاء التحريم من الله فلا يفهم منه إلا التأبيد، فإن كان له حالة إباحة نص عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Past-tense legal wording can establish a new rule or reaffirm an existing one; it need not limit the rule to the past, as in a future-oriented oath.
rows.anchor: وأما أنه صيغة ماض فيخصه فالأفعال التي جاءت يستفاد منها الأحكام الشرعية، وإن كانت بصيغة الماضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase does not make every person’s mother universally forbidden to everyone; generic scope pairs each addressee with his own mother, not all mothers collectively.
rows.anchor: فإنما المفهوم: حرم على كل واحد واحد منكم كل واحدة، واحدة من أم نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The legally prohibited mother is any woman from whom a person descends through birth, whether through his father’s or mother’s line.
rows.anchor: والأم المحرمة شرعا هي كل امرأة رجع نسبك إليها بالولادة من جهة أبيك
